name: Malmö
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Malmö: Öresund cross-border counterparties, construction supply chains and Skåne court asset research.
hero_lede: Malmö is Sweden's third city and the Swedish half of the Öresund region, linked to Copenhagen by bridge since 2000. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the city, coordinating Swedish and Danish counsel and appropriately qualified local professionals where enquiries on the ground are needed.
intro: Malmö is Sweden's third-largest city, with 365,644 residents in the municipality in 2024 and about 780,000 in the metropolitan area. Once dominated by the Kockums shipyard, which stopped building ships in 1986, it has rebuilt itself around services, logistics, education and technology. Business services, health care and motor vehicle trade are the largest employment sectors, and private employers include insurers, food producers, IKEA group companies, transport operators and game developers. More than 270 companies have their headquarters in the city. The Öresund Bridge, opened in July 2000, places Malmö within a cross-border labour market with Copenhagen, and redevelopment of the Western Harbour, Hyllie and Nyhamnen has made the city a major real estate market.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Malmö because its economy straddles two jurisdictions and several fast-growing sectors. Companies contracting across the Öresund need to verify Swedish and Danish counterparties that may be structured on both sides of the border. Large construction and property projects rely on long chains of subcontractors, where Swedish authorities have repeatedly prosecuted tax and bookkeeping offences. Investors in Malmö's real estate, gaming and life sciences businesses want to understand founders, owners and disputes. The city also has high unemployment by Swedish standards and public concern about criminal networks infiltrating legitimate businesses, which raises the bar for counterparty and supplier diligence.

matters.title: Öresund cross-border counterparties
matters.text: Groups operating in Malmö and Copenhagen often split companies, staff and assets between Sweden and Denmark. We combine Bolagsverket records with Danish company register data, court judgments and media from both countries to establish who controls a counterparty, where its assets sit and whether disputes on one side are visible on the other.

matters.title: Construction and subcontractor chains
matters.text: Malmö's large residential and commercial developments rely on multiple tiers of subcontractors. We review subcontractors' registration, F-tax and VAT status where publicly available, board members, business bans, payment remarks obtained lawfully and prior prosecutions, helping main contractors and developers reduce exposure to tax and labour violations.

matters.title: Supplier integrity and criminal infiltration
matters.text: Swedish authorities have highlighted the risk of criminal networks using legitimate companies for fraud and money laundering. We assess suppliers, tenants and partners for indicators such as frequent changes of board members, straw directors, rapid formation and dissolution of companies and links to prior criminal judgments, using lawful public sources.

matters.title: Gaming, technology and life sciences deals
matters.text: Investors and acquirers in Malmö's game studios, software firms and life sciences companies need assurance about founders, ownership, intellectual property and past disputes. We map shareholders and related entities, review court and media records, and identify reputational issues before a transaction or partnership.

matters.title: Asset research for Skåne proceedings
matters.text: Creditors bringing claims before the Malmö District Court or enforcing judgments through the Swedish Enforcement Authority need to know what a debtor holds. We map companies, real property recorded with Lantmäteriet, vehicles and shareholdings, and connected assets in Denmark, so counsel can plan attachment and enforcement.

local_context.title: Malmö District Court
local_context.text: Malmö District Court (Malmö tingsrätt) is the first-instance general court for the city and hears civil, criminal and enforcement-related matters, including substantial economic crime cases brought by the Swedish Economic Crime Authority, such as prosecutions for gross tax, bookkeeping and fraud offences. Swedish court judgments and many case documents are public records that can be requested from the court, subject to secrecy rules. Hearings and filings are in Swedish, and foreign-language evidence normally requires translation.

local_context.title: Court of Appeal for Skåne and Blekinge
local_context.text: The Court of Appeal for Skåne and Blekinge (Hovrätten över Skåne och Blekinge) sits at Hovrättstorget 1 in Malmö and hears appeals from the district courts in its region, including Malmö. Its decisions are an important source when reviewing the litigation history of southern Swedish companies and individuals. The court publishes weekly hearing lists, which can help counsel monitor ongoing matters involving a counterparty.

local_context.title: Economic crime enforcement in Skåne
local_context.text: The Swedish Economic Crime Authority (Ekobrottsmyndigheten) prosecutes economic crime in the region, and its announcements for the Malmö area have covered large frauds, tax schemes using manipulated cash registers and organised tax and bookkeeping offences, with business bans imposed on convicted individuals. Business bans are recorded and can be checked through Bolagsverket, making them a practical diligence check for directors connected to Malmö companies.

local_context.title: Öresund region and Danish records
local_context.text: Many Malmö matters require Danish research as well as Swedish. Danish company information is available through the Central Business Register (CVR), and Danish court and media sources supplement Swedish records. Data protection in both countries follows the GDPR, but access to public documents differs: Sweden's principle of public access gives broad access to court and authority records, while Danish access is more limited. Counsel in both jurisdictions should be involved when evidence crosses the border.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Malmö and works on Malmö matters from Nashville. We agree the objective with the client and its Swedish counsel, and Danish counsel where the matter crosses the Öresund, whether a cross-border counterparty review, a construction supply chain check, an investment or enforcement of a claim. Research draws on Bolagsverket company and business ban records, Lantmäteriet property data obtained lawfully, court judgments requested under the principle of public access, the Danish CVR and Swedish and Danish media, read by native speakers. Personal data is handled under the GDPR and Sweden's supplementary rules. Interviews or site visits are coordinated with appropriately qualified local professionals after counsel review.

faqs.q: Which courts hear disputes involving Malmö companies?
faqs.a: Civil and criminal cases start at Malmö District Court, with appeals to the Court of Appeal for Skåne and Blekinge, which also sits in Malmö, and finally the Supreme Court in Stockholm with leave. Many commercial contracts instead choose arbitration, often under the SCC rules in Stockholm. Swedish counsel advises on forum and procedure.

faqs.q: Can court records in Malmö be obtained?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Under Sweden's principle of public access, judgments and many case documents held by Malmö District Court and the Court of Appeal can be requested, subject to secrecy rules for sensitive information. We request records lawfully, review them with Swedish speakers and use them to build a picture of a counterparty's litigation and criminal history.

faqs.q: How do you check a company operating on both sides of the Öresund?
faqs.a: We search Bolagsverket for Swedish entities and the Danish CVR for Danish ones, then match directors, addresses and owners to identify the full group. Court judgments, enforcement records and media in both countries are reviewed. This reveals whether problems in one jurisdiction are hidden from counterparties in the other.

faqs.q: Can TDSC vet subcontractors on a Malmö construction project?
faqs.a: Yes. We check registration, tax registration status visible in public sources, board composition and changes, business bans, payment remarks obtained lawfully, prosecutions and media coverage for each tier of the supply chain. Findings help the client decide whom to engage and document that reasonable checks were made.

faqs.q: Do you carry out surveillance in Malmö?
faqs.a: No. TDSC does not conduct surveillance or fieldwork itself in Sweden, and the GDPR and Swedish law limit how personal data may be collected and processed. Where observation or interviews are justified, we coordinate appropriately qualified local professionals and agree the method with counsel first. Most Malmö work relies on public records and media research.
